prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Desktop Pet Path", "Select a quick ready-made companion or create a custom pet from your photos."]
1: ["Save Your Companion to Your Account", "Sign in now to save your pet selection and prevent losing pet data."]
2: ["Meet Your Matched Pet Companions", "Based on your preferences, here are the desktop pets best suited for you."]
3: ["Master Your Desktop Pet Controls", "Click pet to interact • Drag to reposition • Right-click for menu"]
4: ["Sign in with your primary account to keep and sync your existing pets across devices."]
5: ["Clear photos work best. You can also pick a premade pet model if custom pet generation takes too long."]
6: ["Rendering Your Desktop Pet", "Setup takes under 30 seconds. Ensure your app has permission to display on your desktop background."]
7: ["Fastest Setup (30 Seconds)"]
8: ["We will notify you on your desktop as soon as your pet is ready to play."]
9: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Your companion is officially ready to move onto your desktop."]
